correctness.rationale: The failure identity follows from an exact partition of survivor subsets. Complete inverse Prüfer enumeration covers all labeled trees on 2–7 vertices and all protected choices; the exact coefficientwise comparison proves universal optima on every smaller tree. All 840 seven-vertex exceptions have the subdivided three-star structure, whose two undominated root polynomials cross exactly once at the stated algebraic probability. Standalone direct 64-state survival enumeration checks the witness at four rational parameter values.

evidence: Amin–Siegrist–Slater analyze expected connected pair number across graph designs; the Ugurlu abstract concerns vertex attack objectives and states that tree-restricted behavior is left open.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither an expectation of pairs nor all-survivor connectivity fixes the probability that any operational edge exists under protection of exactly one vertex. General root-dependent dominance could in principle imply this, but no such stronger matching theorem was identified.

value.rationale: The event of retaining any locally adjacent pair captures minimal remaining connectivity in fragmented habitat; the sharp first patch count at which conservation targeting must depend on environment, complete smallest-obstruction class, and exact switching threshold give a motivated boundary rather than an arbitrary tiny numerical improvement. Limitations prevent interpreting it as real-world viability.
